newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria, EU discuss association deal.
newsitem.headline: Algeria, EU discuss association deal.

text.p: Algerian and European Union officials on Monday started talks in Algiers on an association trade accord expected to be finalised in October, Algerian state-run radio said.
The accord, offering financial, social and cultural links between Algeria and the 15-nation European Union, will replace a pact in place since 1978.
The two sides began a first round of negotiations on the deal in March.

The radio, setting the tone for the present round of talks, said Algeria wanted to bargain hard, on the basis of its huge market potential, and strike a far-reaching deal with the EU, including a clause over the free movement of people.
"Algeria aims to reach an accord on the basis of a true partnership allowing the transfer of industrial technology and shared development," the radio said in a commentary.
Algeria, with 29 million people, has been battered by civil strife since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
About 60,000 people have died since then in the violence in the country which helps meet much of Europe's oil and gas needs.

Algeria is preparing a parliamentary election to be held on June 5 which the authorities say will lay to rest doubts about the government's eagerness to establish a multi-party democracy and pull the country into stability.
